core_obligations: Separable case (proof lines 18043-18048): if L/K is separable then L is a filtered colimit of smooth K-algebras, so the general smooth base change lemma applies directly and gives the pullback statement.

Reduce the general case to the separable one (proof lines 18049-18059): let K' and L' be the perfect closures of K and L; the morphisms Spec(K') -> Spec(K) and Spec(L') -> Spec(L) are universal homeomorphisms, so topological invariance of etale cohomology gives (T_{K'})_etale = T_etale and (T_{L'})_etale = (T_L)_etale, and similarly for S.
Conclude (proof lines 18060-18063): this reduces the lemma to the extension L'/K', which is separable because K' and L' are perfect, and hence covered by the first case.
proof_roadmap: Handle a separable extension by the smooth base change lemma for filtered colimits of smooth algebras.
Pass to perfect closures, using topological invariance to identify the etale sites.
Apply the separable case to the extension of perfect fields.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the pushforward of a torsion complex with orders invertible in the base commutes with an extension of base fields (statement lines 18031-18040). The proof (proof lines 18042-18063) handles separable extensions by the smooth base change lemma for filtered colimits of smooth algebras, and reduces the general case to that one by passing to perfect closures, where topological invariance identifies the etale sites. H2: one base change application plus one reduction, written out.
